etymologies.etymologyHTML:
Origin disputed. Wikipedia lists many possible etymologies, of which the most widely accepted is that it is an abbreviation of oll/orl korrect, a comical spelling of all correct, which first appeared in print in The Boston Morning Post on March 23, 1839, as part of a fad for similar fanciful abbreviations in the United States during the late 1830s. The expression became popular through its use in the presidential campaign of Martin Van Buren in 1840, who was nicknamed Old Kinderhook, and then slowly acquired other meanings.

The Choctaw word oke, okeh (“it is so”), common in Choctaw translations of the Bible, could also explain OK's variety of affirmative definitions. Additionally, okeh was the most common etymology of okay in dictionaries until the 1960s, and linguistically predates Boston's O.K.. However, this theory suffers from the fact that the Choctaw language was relatively obscure and generally spoken (sometimes in a pidgin form) mainly with African-American slaves.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To approve; to accept; to acquiesce to.
(transitive, computing) To confirm by activating a button marked OK.

quote.citation: 2001, Mike Collins, Pro Tools: Practical Recording, Editing and Mixing for Music Production:
quote.text: Type a suitable name for your Marker and OK the dialogue box.

quote.citation: 2008, Martin Evening, Adobe Photoshop CS4 for Photographers:
quote.text: When you OK the crop, the image size will be adjusted to match the front image resolution.

quote.citation: 1869, Louisa M[ay] Alcott, Little Women: […], part second, Boston, Mass.: Roberts Brothers, →OCLC:
quote.text: One of us must marry well. Meg didn't, Jo won't, Beth can't yet, so I shall, and make everything okay all round.

definitions.definition: Satisfied (with); willing to accept a state of affairs.

quote.citation: 2012, Roni Jay, The 10 Most Important Things You Can Do For Your Children:
quote.text: If you leave the kids in the creche for one morning on your week's holiday, and they are OK with that, then it's fine.

definitions.definition: In good health or a good emotional state.

quote.citation: 2022 October 25, L. J. Shrum, Elena Fumagalli, Tina M. Lowrey, “Coping with loneliness through consumption”, in Journal of Consumer Psychology, volume 33, number 2, →DOI, page 452:
quote.text: In France, the French postal service La Poste provides a subscription service in which postal workers visit elderly subscribers to make sure they are okay, do not need anything, and provide brief social interaction.

definitions.definition: Used to indicate acknowledgement or acceptance.

quote.text:
Come by this afternoon. — Okay.
Audio (US):(file)

definitions.definition: (computing) Used to dismiss a dialog box or confirm a prompt.
Used to introduce a sentence in order to draw attention to the importance of what is being said.
Used in turn-taking, serving as a request to the speaker to grant the turn to the interrupter.
Used to sarcastically or sardonically indicate agreement with the previous statement.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: Possibly a shortening of Chinese 卡拉OK. (Can this etymology be sourced?)
